For days, snow had blocked the road to the village. The flour seller could not come up, and no one could go down.

The flour sack in Hadi's house grew lighter day by day, until Hadi could hear the bottom of it whenever his mother scooped from it.

On the evening of the fifth day, Hadi's mother took one single loaf out of the oven. Then she shook the sack over the dough bowl, and nothing came out.

She put the loaf on the tray between Hadi and Sumayya and said, "This is our dinner tonight, and the morning is in Allah's hands."

Hadi reached out for the loaf. He had been hungry since noon.

Before he could break it, there was a soft knock at the door.

Hadi opened it, and there was their neighbour Abu Subhi, an old man who lived alone at the end of the alley. His beard was white with snow, and his hands were trembling.

He said, "My son, do you have a piece of bread? I haven't tasted anything since yesterday."

Hadi looked at the loaf, and then at his mother.

His mother said in a quiet voice, "It's your loaf, Hadi. Do what you think is right."

Sumayya looked at the loaf and said nothing.

Hadi stood there for a long time. Then he picked up the tray and held it out to Abu Subhi.

The old man said, "And what about you?" Hadi said, "There are three of us to keep each other warm, and you're all alone."

Abu Subhi took the loaf, made a long du'a for them, and walked off through the snow to his house.

Then Hadi's mother brought out a little bundle with a handful of dried figs she had been saving. The three of them shared them, and went to sleep.

In the morning the men of the village dug a path through the snow, and the flour seller came up with his mule.

Abu Subhi got to him first, took out all the money he had in his pocket, and said, "The first sack goes to Hadi's house."

The seller brought the sack to Hadi's door, with Abu Subhi beside him leaning on his stick.

The old man said to Hadi's mother, "I had money but no bread. You had only one loaf, and you gave it away. So this is for that."

That morning, Hadi's mother kneaded lots and lots of dough, and she sent Hadi with the very first loaf out of the oven to Abu Subhi's house.

And from that day on, Hadi stopped by the old man's house every morning on his way.

﴿وَيُؤْثِرُونَ عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِهِمْ وَلَوْ كَانَ بِهِمْ خَصَاصَةٌ﴾

📖 Al-Hashr 9. This is a tale told as a parable; it did not happen to anyone in particular.
